title: Perf hypothesis vault (backfill notes)
content:
Quick personal vault for hypotheses I want to backfill from last three weeks of noisy runs. This is messy — mostly timestamps, quick checks, and next steps. Use as a scratch brain-dump not a final write-up.

Context and motive:
- Running hosted beta with mixed small/large payloads; noticing intermittent p99 spikes tied to token merging and cold KV hits.
- Hypothesis set: (H1) prefix/KV priming cut tail by >30% for short-context requests; (H2) batching timeout tradeoffs cause mid-tier p95 jumps under bursty ingress; (H3) small-request packing amplification when mixed with long sequences degrades throughput via scheduler stalls.

Experiment summary (cheap, quick runs):
- infra: single dedicated gpu (A100-sim), runtime v0.9.4+dev, model: llama-ish quantized 4-bit variant, context limit 2048.
- traffic shape: synthetic Poisson baseline, 10% heavy (1k tokens), 90% short (16–64 tokens).
- measurements: 60s windows, 3 warmup windows prior to capture.

Raw run table (hand collated):
Run | config | qps (observed) | p50 ms | p95 ms | p99 ms | quick note
R1   | no-prime, batch-t=10ms       | 230 | 26  | 120 | 340 | many cold kv hits, spikes every ~8s
R2   | kv-prime 1MB cache           | 410 | 22  | 85  | 160 | tail reduced ~53% vs R1
R3   | batch-t=2ms, no-prime       | 290 | 24  | 140 | 380 | lower latency p50 but p99 worse than R1
R4   | batch-t=2ms + kv-prime      | 560 | 20  | 78  | 150 | best end-to-end for mixed traffic
R5   | small-pack disabled + prime | 480 | 21  | 95  | 210 | packing disabled drops throughput on heavy fraction

Preliminary conclusions (not final):
- KV prefix priming yields large wins for p95/p99 in short-heavy mixes (H1 supported). Benefit scales with prime size but diminishing returns past ~1MB.
- Aggressive lowering of batch timeout (2ms) reduces p50 but can widen p99 unless priming present (H2 partially supported). The runtime's continuous-batch fallback appears to create microqueues that time out and spike latencies.
- Request packing (small->large) improves GPU throughput for heavy sequences but introduces scheduling jitter when small short requests interleave — need packing-aware fairness. H3 supported conditionally.

Notes about instrumentation gaps:
- Tracing not correlating refreshes of KV with token-level latency; need to emit KV-miss span with context-length tag.
- Sampling TTL for p99 currently 1s; increase to 10s for better tail fidelity in burst windows.

Actionable next steps / todo:
- [ ] Add span: kv:miss:size and wire it through tracing (linked GH PR GH-PR-789).
- [ ] Run a controlled grid over prime sizes {128KB, 512KB, 1MB, 4MB} with mixed traffic generator, 5x 2m windows. Assign Jun to orchestrate.
- [ ] Experiment with packer fairness: implement simple weight = 1/(seq_len+8) as stopgap; measure fairness and throughput.
- [ ] Bake a reproducible script and attach to Confluence draft (CONFLUENCE-1234) before next weekly sync.

Random observations / scribbles:
- Cold/gateway spikes often align with a host eviction event timestamp in node logs ~ +7s after surge; correlation not causal yet.
- When prime size >2MB warmup cost visible: initial ramp latency increases but steady-state tail is lower. Tradeoff for bursty short-lived clients.
- Thought: auto-adapt prime size by moving EWMA of short-request ratio -> prime_size mapping. Prototype as a runtime hint, not auto-change.

Open questions:
- What is the memory and eviction policy interaction if we keep per-tenant primes? (Need SRE input)
- Does quantized-kv layout affect priming cost? (ask applied-ml to run microbench)

End notes: keep this file as working vault for the week. If something is promising, migrate to a more formal runbook under shared_drives/engineering/serving-runtime/benchmarks.

-- Omar
